stage_fields.problem_definition: Given a sparse scRNA-seq UMI count matrix X (cells x genes) and a technical dropout process that zeroes some true counts, recover the counterfactual true count at each dropout position, on a CPU-only Python/scanpy stack without deep learning, so downstream differential / trajectory / marker analyses are not biased by technical zeros -- while transparently reporting the regime (MAR vs MNAR) in which the recovery is identifiable.
stage_fields.estimand: The counterfactual true transcript count y*_{c,g} at a position (cell c, gene g) whose observed value is zero due to technical dropout (mask M_{c,g}=0), over the target population of future scRNA-seq experiments on the same tissue/platform family -- the count that would have been observed absent technical dropout. This is a per-position counterfactual count, NOT a global 'denoised matrix' summary.

symbols.X: observed counts, X in Z_+^{n_cells x n_genes}; entry X[c,g] >= 0
symbols.M: observation mask, M in {0,1}^{n_cells x n_genes}; M[c,g]=1 if the entry was observed (X[c,g] is a realized count, possibly 0), M[c,g]=0 if it was technically dropped out. NOTE: M is NOT observed directly in real data -- a real zero could be 'true zero + observed' or 'dropped out'. For evaluation (mask-then-impute) M is known by construction; for inference M is imputed from the dropout model.
symbols.W: cell-similarity graph weights, row-normalized kNN graph on cells (cosine on log-normalized expression in PCA space), zero diagonal
symbols.L: graph Laplacian of W, L = I - (W + W^T)/2 (symmetric normalized)
symbols.U: eigenvector matrix of L (graph Fourier basis); U[:, :k] are the k lowest-frequency eigenvectors
symbols.Y: recovered true counts, Y in R_+^{n_cells x n_genes}; Y[c,g] is the estimate of y*_{c,g}
symbols.lib: per-cell library size (total observed counts), lib[c] = sum_g X[c,g]
symbols.beta_dropout: logistic dropout slope coupling dropout prob to (log) true expression -- the MNAR coupling parameter; beta_dropout=0 is MAR
symbols.mask_obs: boolean evaluation mask used in mask-then-impute, distinct from the inferred M

stage_fields.objective_or_likelihood: TREATS M AS LATENT (not observed). The mask M[c,g] is never observed in real data -- a realized zero could be a true biological zero (M=1, X=0) or a technical dropout (M=0, X=0) -- so the objective marginalizes M under the joint model. The complete-data log-likelihood (with soft posterior responsibilities r[c,g] = P(M[c,g]=0 | X, Y, alpha, beta) computed in an explicit mask-E-step) is:  Q = sum_{c,g} [ (1-r[c,g]) * ( log P(X=0 | Y, M=1) + log P(M=1 | Y) ) + r[c,g] * ( log P(M=0 | Y) ) ]  -  lambda * tr(Y^T L Y)   where P(X | Y, M=1) is NB(mean=Y, dispersion=phi[g]) (so P(X=0|Y,M=1) is the NB-at-zero probability -- a true biological zero gets nonzero likelihood), P(M=0 | Y) = sigmoid(alpha + beta*log1p(Y)) is the logistic dropout, and lambda * tr(Y^T L Y) is the graph-Laplacian smoothness penalty on the FULL Y matrix (the penalty applies at observed AND masked entries; at observed entries the NB data-fit anchors Y to X while the penalty regularizes, standard graph-signal tradeoff). Lambda >= 0 is the smoothness weight (equivalently a graph low-pass bandwidth). Y at masked entries is constrained to span(U[:, :k]) -- the top-k lowest-graph-frequency eigenvectors -- which makes the smoothness penalty finite-rank and the masked-entry recovery a projection onto a k-dim subspace. This marginalize-M formulation is the non-deep-learning analog of what scVI/DCA amortize with a VAE; we keep the logistic-dropout coupling explicit so beta_dropout is interpretable as the MNAR self-diagnostic (vs MAGIC which has no likelihood, vs scVI which buries the coupling in a deep prior).
stage_fields.identifiability: Two-level honesty. (1) UNDER MNAR (beta != 0): NOT identifiable without an external instrument. A low observed count and a high-but-dropped-out count produce identical evidence (X=0 in both), so Y at masked entries is confounded with the dropout-model parameters -- no estimator can uniquely recover it (trap T6). (2) UNDER MAR (beta=0) -- a NECESSARY CORRECTION to the naive read: Y at masked entries is NOT data-identified; it is PRIOR-DOMINATED. The NB data-likelihood term contributes zero gradient at masked entries (X=0 there and the mask posterior r is what carries the dropout model's say, not direct count evidence); the masked-entry recovery is pinned ALMOST ENTIRELY by the graph-smoothness prior + the observed-neighbor structure. So under MAR the imputation is WELL-DEFINED (a unique regularized optimum exists given lambda, k, phi) but it is identification-by-assumption (the smoothness prior + the dropout-marginalized posterior on M), NOT identification-by-data at the masked positions themselves. The honest framing: under MAR the masked-entry estimate is a regularized kNN-graph-smoothed imputation (mathematically kin to MAGIC/scImpute in the MAR limit) whose bias is governed by lambda and the cell-type homogeneity of the graph neighborhoods (FB3); under MNAR it is confounded on top of that. IDENTIFIABILITY IS RESTORED only by an external instrument (spike-ins / ERCC with known true counts subject to the same dropout; or paired full-length + droplet on the same cells) that separately identifies the dropout curve and pins Y at spike-in positions, propagating through the graph. The method's contribution is NOT claiming data-identification under MAR; it is (a) making the prior-dominance explicit, (b) jointly fitting beta_dropout and reporting its CI as a REGIME INDICATOR (not a tight data-identified estimate -- see beta_dropout caveat in assumptions), and (c) flagging the MNAR regime rather than papering over it. This is the novelty axis vs MAGIC/scVI which give NO identifiability boundary at all.

failure_boundaries.condition: Dropout is genuinely MNAR (|beta_dropout| large -- dropout probability strongly coupled to low true expression), AND no external instrument is available.
failure_boundaries.mechanism: Under MNAR the masked-entry count is not identifiable (see identifiability): the NB likelihood at observed entries cannot distinguish a genuinely low-expressing cell from a dropped-out high-expressing cell. The graph-smoothness prior then smooths toward neighbors, which under MNAR systematically over-imputes (drags zeros up toward the local mean). Recovery RMSE grows roughly linearly in |beta_dropout|. The method's correct behavior here is to DETECT this (large fitted |beta_dropout|) and flag it, NOT to silently return the over-smoothed estimate.
failure_boundaries.guard: Report adata.uns['mnar_flag'] = (|beta_dropout_hat| > tau_mnar) and adata.uns['impute_confidence'] scaled by 1/(1+|beta_dropout_hat|).

failure_boundaries.condition: Ultra-sparse regime: cells with < 500 genes detected (very shallow libraries / poor-quality cells).
failure_boundaries.mechanism: The kNN cell-similarity graph collapses onto a few high-degree hubs (the cosine / PCA representation is dominated by noise when few genes are nonzero); the low-frequency graph subspace is too small to carry the signal. The smoothness prior then over-smooths -- erasing real biological variation across cell types -- and imputation degrades to global-mean fill. The graph-spectral recovery has no informative low-frequency basis to project onto.
failure_boundaries.guard: Build the graph on cells passing a min_genes filter (scanpy.pp.filter_cells(min_genes=500)); for sub-threshold cells, fall back to per-gene observed-mean imputation and set adata.obs['impute_confidence']=0 for them; exclude them from neighborhood-graph construction.

failure_boundaries.condition: Cell-type heterogeneity is large relative to the graph bandwidth -- e.g. lineage-transition genes whose expression is high-frequency on the cell graph (sharp changes across a developmental boundary), OR cell-type-composition shift across donors (a held-out donor with a different type mixture).
failure_boundaries.mechanism: The graph-low-pass / Laplacian-smoothness assumption treats cell-graph-high-frequency variation as noise and suppresses it. For genes that genuinely vary sharply across nearby cells (transition / immediate-early genes), this is signal, not noise -- the low-pass step attenuates real biology and imputation underestimates the true heterogeneity. Composition shift (audit-driven): under cross-donor type-mixture differences, a held-out donor's dropout positions are smoothed toward the TRAINING-set type mixture, type-blurring the imputation -- the recovered count is a type-averaged value, not the counterfactual for the cell's own type. This is the standard bias-variance tradeoff of any smoothing imputer (MAGIC has it worse; scVI amortizes it).
failure_boundaries.guard: Per-gene graph-bandwidth diagnostic: compute the graph-frequency spectrum of each gene's observed signal; for genes whose energy is concentrated in high graph-frequencies, widen the bandwidth (increase k) or skip the low-pass and use NB-mean fill. Report adata.var['graph_bandwidth']. For composition shift: restrict smoothing to within-type neighborhoods (carry a cell-type label per node; build a type-blocked graph), and add an inter-batch anchor step for new donors.

failure_boundaries.condition: Sequencing-depth confound: library sizes differ across cells by >5x and the cell graph is built on un-normalized or improperly normalized counts.
failure_boundaries.mechanism: Without depth normalization the kNN graph clusters cells by total UMI count (a technical artifact), not by biology. The smoothness prior then propagates depth-correlated signal, and imputation reproduces depth differences as if they were biological -- a confound. NB dispersion is also mis-fit if library size is not modeled.
failure_boundaries.guard: Always normalize before graph construction (scanpy.pp.normalize_total + log1p + scale); include library size lib[c] as an offset in the NB mean (mean = lib[c] * exp(...) per cell); build the graph on PCA of the normalized matrix, never on raw X.

stage_fields.complexity: Per outer iteration: graph eigendecomposition is the bottleneck. Full eigendecomposition is O(n_cells^3) and caps at ~1e4 cells. For larger n_cells we use the truncated eigenbasis of the LOWEST-frequency eigenvectors via eigsh on (cI - L) with which='LM' (largest-magnitude of the shifted operator = smallest eigenvalue of L) -- this is PURE MATVEC Lanczos, O(k * n_cells * n_neighbors) per matvec, NO shift-invert factorization (which='SM' on L directly would require a sparse factorization of L with O(n^1.5)-ish fill-in and dominate RAM at 1e5 cells -- explicitly avoided). Per-gene low-pass projection: O(n_cells * k) once U[:, :k] is fixed. NB M-step (phi, lib offset): O(n_cells * n_genes). Newton dropout update (alpha, beta): O(n_cells * n_genes). E-step inner NB gradient step: NOT globally convex (NB log-lik in its mean is only locally concave) -- use a damped Newton with line search in a trust region around current Y; 2-3 inner steps empirically, observed convergence reported (not claimed). Total: O(k * n_cells * n_neighbors + n_cells * n_genes * T_outer) for T_outer EM iterations after eigendecomposition precompute. Memory: X stored SPARSE (CSR, ~n_cells*n_neighbors nonzero) -- NOT dense; Y and P are dense O(n_cells*n_genes) float32 each; the count+recovery matrices are the memory bottleneck. For n_cells=1e5, n_genes=2e4: X sparse ~ few hundred MB, Y dense ~8 GB, P dense ~8 GB, eigenbasis O(n_cells*k)~25 MB -- realistic peak ~20-24 GB at 1e5 cells (the earlier '8-16 GB' estimate was optimistic and is corrected here); cap the dense path at ~3e4 cells (peak ~6 GB) and chunk genes above that. EM converges in 10-50 outer iterations (monotone ascent on the mask-marginalized Q lower bound of L); stop when relative change in L < 1e-4.
stage_fields.mathematical_abstraction: Masked signal recovery on a cell-similarity graph with a negative-binomial count likelihood, jointly fit with a logistic dropout model. Rejected: (a) zero-inflated latent inference via VAE -- forces a deep generative family (user forbids DL) and buries the recovery structure + identifiability in a latent prior, making the MNAR failure mode opaque; (b) pure matrix completion -- cells x genes is NOT low-rank in the compressed-sensing sense, the smoothness is on the cell-GRAPH not the matrix, so CS sparsity priors are a weaker match; (c) MAGIC-style unconditional graph diffusion -- no count likelihood, no dropout model, no identifiability boundary. The graph-signal + NB + joint-dropout abstraction is selected because it keeps the failure boundary transparent, is CPU-native (graph Laplacian eigenbasis is a one-time precompute), and the joint dropout fit gives a self-diagnostic for the MNAR boundary that prior imputers lack.
assumptions: Count distribution: X[c,g] ~ NegativeBinomial(mean = lib[c] * q[c,g], dispersion = phi[g]) -- NB per gene, with library size as offset. This is the standard droplet scRNA count model (Svensson 2020 shows droplet UMI counts are well fit by a single NB, no extra zero-inflation term needed).

Missingness mechanism IS THE KEY ASSUMPTION and is NOT defaulted to MNAR. Droplet scRNA zeros are a MIX of (i) true biological zeros (gene not expressed in that cell -- observed zero, M=1, X=0) and (ii) technical dropouts (gene expressed but not captured -- M=0, X=0). HONEST REFRAME (audit-driven): for low-expression genes a realized zero is jointly caused -- low true count AND capture failure under ~10% efficiency -- so 'technical dropout' is a modelling convenience for the stochastic-capture tail of a low NB mean, NOT a cleanly separable per-entry process. The method ASSUMES MAR (beta_dropout=0) for the primary estimator -- dropout probability depends on observable quantities (library size, gene mean) but NOT on the unobserved true count -- and TREATS MNAR as a self-diagnosed failure boundary (FB1), NOT a silent assumption. Defaulting to MNAR is the trap (T2); defaulting to MCAR is equally wrong. We justify MAR per-platform by citing Svensson (droplet UMI counts fit NB without zero-inflation).

beta_dropout IDENTIFIABILITY CAVEAT (audit-driven): beta_dropout is NOT tightly data-identified under MAR. The mask posterior r[c,g] = P(M=0|X,Y,alpha,beta) is what the dropout-model fit sees, and under MAR the per-entry biological/technical-zero ambiguity limits how informative X is about beta; so the fitted beta_dropout_hat CI is a REGIME INDICATOR (does |beta_hat| clearly exceed tau_mnar with a tight CI?), not a precise estimate. The mnar_flag is therefore a coarse detector; we pre-register its Type I/II error on a known-MNAR simulator (downsample a full-length dataset with depth-coupled dropout) and report observed sensitivity/specificity rather than claiming a calibrated posterior. An external instrument (spike-ins / ERCC, or a paired dilution series) RESTORES tight identification of beta_dropout; the absence of such a calibrant degrades the diagnostic to a flag, not a measurement.

Graph-smoothness: true counts are smooth on the cell-similarity graph (cells close on the graph have similar expression) -- violated for lineage-transition genes (FB3) AND violated under cell-type-composition shift across donors (a held-out donor with a different type mixture has its dropout positions smoothed toward the training-set mixture, type-blurring the imputation -- audit-driven addition).
Library size is a known offset (sum of observed counts) -- not estimated.

Batch / cohort structure (carried from data-audit) is modeled as a known covariate; the graph is built WITHIN batch where possible, or batch is included as a blocking covariate. For a NEW donor whose batch has no graph node, an inter-batch anchor step (mutual-NN with a calibration gate, or scanorama/harmony alignment) attaches it; without that step the new-donor generalization claim is bounded by batch alignment quality.

UPSTREAM DECONFINING (audit-driven): ambient/cell-free RNA contamination (SoupX/DecontX/CellBender territory) and dissociation-induced stress signatures (FOS, JUN, HSP, immediate-early genes) are assumed REMOVED or FLAGGED before imputation runs. The imputer would otherwise 'recover' ambient counts and stress-gene expression at dropout positions, biasing the very marker analyses it claims to protect. The pipeline contract states X is post-decontamination + stress-genes-flagged.

DOWNSTREAM-USE CONTESTATION (audit-driven): the motivation 'imputed counts feed DE/trajectory/marker analyses without bias' is CONTESTED in the field (Andrews & Hemberg 2018, F1000Research; Zhang et al. on imputation-induced artefacts) -- imputed values are model-dependent and can inflate DE false positives/negatives. The method does NOT claim imputation-then-DE is bias-free; it claims the mnar_flag/impute_confidence let a user SEE when imputed counts are unreliable. Recommended downstream use: DE on imputed counts only when mnar_flag is clear and impute_confidence is high; otherwise prefer latent-space (scVI-style) or pseudobulk-at-donor DE. This is a stated LIMITATION, not a hidden premise.
stage_fields.cross_domain_inspiration: Engaged, two domains outside single-cell imputation: (1) GRAPH SIGNAL PROCESSING -- graph-Laplacian low-pass / graph-Fourier filtering as the recovery operator (the cell-similarity graph is the native signal domain; smoothness = graph bandwidth). Spark selected: truncated graph-Fourier basis U[:, :k] as the low-pass projection. (2) MISSING-DATA / CAUSAL INFERENCE -- the identifiability theory of MNAR (the classic result that MNAR without an instrument is not identifiable), operationalized as a JOINT logistic dropout model whose fitted slope beta_dropout is a self-diagnostic for the failure boundary. Spark selected: jointly-fit logistic dropout coupling -> the magnitude of beta_dropout IS the MNAR detector. Discarded sparks: compressed sensing (sparsity prior is a weaker match -- expression is not sparse on the cell graph in the CS sense); Bayesian search theory (no search problem here). Cross-domain engagement is justified because each spark gives a concrete axis of improvement (graph-Fourier = CPU-native scalable recovery; joint dropout = transparent identifiability diagnostic) -- NOT forced to satisfy a novelty quota.
stage_fields.proposed_algorithm: Graph-spectral NB imputation with joint dropout self-diagnosis (gsNB-Dropout). Steps: (1) PREPROCESS: scanpy.pp.filter_cells(min_genes=500) -> remove FB2-susceptible cells (or flag them); scanpy.pp.normalize_total(target_sum=1e4); scanpy.pp.log1p; scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes(n_top_genes=2000); scanpy.pp.scale; scanpy.pp.pca(n_comps=50). (2) GRAPH: scanpy.pp.neighbors(n_neighbors=15, use_rep='X_pca', metric='cosine') -> adata.obsp['connectivities'] is W; compute symmetric normalized Laplacian L = I - (W+W^T)/2. (3) EIGENBASIS: scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh(c*sp.eye(n) - L, k=64, which='LM') where c > max eigenvalue of L -> the k LARGEST-magnitude eigenvectors of the shifted operator are the k SMALLEST-eigenvalue (lowest-frequency) eigenvectors of L = U[:, :64]; pure-matvec Lanczos, no shift-invert factorization (full eigendecomposition only for n_cells < 1e4). (4) DISPERSION PRE-FIT: per-gene NB dispersion phi[g] fit on observed non-zero entries with library offset (method-of-moments). (5) EM LOOP WITH LATENT M (initialize Y = observed-count mean imputation at masked entries, beta=0): MASK-E-STEP = compute soft responsibilities r[c,g] = P(M=0 | X, Y, alpha, beta) under the joint NB+logistic-dropout model (this is the latent-mask treatment -- real zeros get a posterior probability of being biological vs technical); Y-M-STEP = given r and (alpha,beta), solve the smoothness-regularized expected-NB-MLE for Y with Y[:,masked] constrained to span(U[:, :k]) -- damped Newton with line search in a trust region (NOT claimed convex: NB log-lik is only locally concave in its mean), 2-3 inner steps; DROPOUT-M-STEP = given Y and r, update (alpha, beta) by Newton on the logistic dropout likelihood; iterate until relative change in the mask-marginalized Q < 1e-4 (10-50 iters). (6) DIAGNOSE: read off beta_dropout_hat and its CI; if |beta_dropout_hat| > tau_mnar set adata.uns['mnar_flag']=True and adata.uns['impute_confidence'] scaled down by 1/(1+|beta_dropout_hat|); emit adata.layers['imputed'] = Y, adata.layers['mask_posterior'] = r, and adata.layers['impute_variance'] (from the Laplacian precision inverse on the low-pass subspace).
stage_fields.optimization_or_inference: Generalized EM (mask-marginalized) -- M is LATENT, marginalized in the mask-E-step. The Q function (expected complete-data log-lik over the mask posterior r) is maximized in three coordinated blocks: (a) MASK-E-STEP: r[c,g] = P(M=0|X,Y,alpha,beta) under the joint NB+logistic model -- closed-form per entry given current (Y, alpha, beta). (b) Y-M-STEP: solve max_Y [ sum_{c,g} (1-r[c,g]) * log NB(X=0|Y,phi) + smoothness ] - lambda*tr(Y^T L Y) with Y[:,masked] constrained to span(U[:,:k]). Per-gene: project the NB-gradient onto the low-pass subspace, take a proximal step on the Laplacian penalty (closed-form multiplication by (I + lambda*Lambda_k)^-1 where Lambda_k is the diagonal of kept eigenvalues), then 2-3 damped-Newton inner steps for NB nonlinearity (NOT globally convex -- NB log-lik in its mean is only locally concave; trust region around current Y; observed convergence reported, not claimed). (c) DROPOUT-M-STEP: Newton on the logistic dropout likelihood for (alpha, beta) given (Y, r) -- convex (logistic), 3-5 Newton steps, line-searched. Outer loop: monotone non-decrease of Q (GEM / MM-style), converges to a coordinate-wise optimum; NOT guaranteed global -- initialization-sensitive (initialize Y at masked entries from per-gene observed-mean, phi from method-of-moments, beta=0). Stop when relative change in Q < 1e-4 or 50 outer iters.
stage_fields.simulation_dgp: DGP: (a) sample latent cell states z_c on a 2D Swiss-roll / tree manifold (n_cells in {500, 2000, 10000}); (b) assign genes to manifolds with varying graph-frequency (80% low-freq smooth, 20% high-freq transition -- to probe FB3); (c) generate true counts Y*[c,g] ~ NB(mean = lib[c] * softmax(z_c . B[:, g]), dispersion = phi[g]); (d) generate mask M[c,g] ~ Bernoulli(1 - sigmoid(alpha + beta * log1p(Y*[c,g]))) with beta swept over {0 (MAR/null), -0.5, -1.0, -2.0 (strong MNAR/adversarial)}; zero out X where M=0. Regimes: NULL = set Y*[c,g]=0 at a random subset (true zeros) -- method MUST NOT hallucinate nonzero counts there, report false-imputation rate. ADVERSARIAL = beta=-2 (strong MNAR) + n_genes_detected in {100, 500, 2000} (drives FB1 and FB2). ORACLE = give method the true M and noiseless Y* at observed entries -> upper bound on recovery. TRIVIAL = global-mean and copy-observed imputation -> lower bound. Sweep: beta (dropout coupling) x lambda (smoothness weight) x n_detected (sparsity) x k (graph bandwidth) -> plot recovery RMSE vs beta to locate the FB1 break point, and vs n_detected to locate FB2.
stage_fields.benchmark_protocol: Competitors (same preprocessing, same held-out expression-INDEPENDENT mask, same compute budget, same seeds, SAME HYPERPARAMETER-SEARCH BUDGET): NAIVE baselines (Cat 5, MANDATORY) -- all-zero imputation, global-mean imputation, per-gene-mean, kNN-mean (k=15), copy-observed (no imputation); SOTA (Cat 1 functional substitutes) -- scVI (v1.2+, deep generative, run on CPU), MAGIC (v2, graph diffusion), SAVER (v1.1, denoising), DCA (ZINB autoencoder). Versions pinned in requirements.txt. HYPERPARAMETER FAIRNESS (audit-driven): each method -- proposed AND competitors -- receives the SAME hyperparameter-search budget (e.g. 30 Optuna trials, 3-fold inner CV, objective = held-out RMSE on the same mask); search logs reported; no method runs at package defaults while another is tuned (that would rig the comparison). Protocol: mask 20% of nonzero observed entries per cell with a Bernoulli(p=0.2) mask INDEPENDENT of expression magnitude (NOT a magnitude-coupled mask -- trap T3); leakage check: regress mask-indicator on log-expression, require |coef| < 0.05. FIT-SCOPE (audit-driven): ALL per-gene NB dispersion phi[g] and per-cell library-size / normalization factors are fit on TRAIN entries ONLY (unmasked), then FROZEN before imputation of held-out entries -- held-out entries are excluded from all parameter estimation (no test-on-train leak). Metrics: RMSE on held-out counts, Pearson r on held-out entries, false-imputation rate in null regime, downstream-cluster ARI recovery (Leiden on imputed vs on ground truth), runtime, peak memory. Fairness: identical mask generation, identical dispersion pre-fit (on TRAIN), compute-matched (cap wall-clock per method), 5 seeds. ORACLE-AS-CEILING (audit-driven): the ORACLE regime (true M + noiseless Y* at observed entries) is reported ONLY as a labeled information-theoretic upper-bound reference line, NEVER as a competing method in the headline comparison table. Per-regime reporting: report metrics split by beta regime and by n_detected regime so FB1/FB2 are visible in the table, not hidden in an aggregate. PER-ESTIMAND METRICS (audit-driven): (i) IN-SAMPLE entry-level imputation error -- RMSE/Pearson on re-masked entries, its own table; (ii) NEW-DONOR generalization -- donor-level k-fold, RMSE/Pearson on cells of FULLY HELD-OUT donors with NO re-masking, its own SEPARATE table; the two estimands are NOT conflated.
stage_fields.novelty_or_utility_basis: Utility first, novelty explicit. Novelty locus: NEW INFERENCE MECHANISM + NEW IDENTIFIABILITY DIAGNOSTIC for this estimand. (1) Graph-spectral low-pass as the recovery operator (vs MAGIC's unconditional diffusion / scVI's amortized deep prior) -- CPU-native, one-time eigendecomposition precompute, transparent bandwidth parameter. (2) JOINT logistic dropout fit whose slope beta_dropout IS the MNAR self-diagnostic -- prior imputers fit dropout but do not turn the fitted coupling into a per-sample identifiability flag. (3) Explicit identifiability analysis (MAR yes / MNAR no) that prior imputers OMIT. Tier T2 -- defensibly better on >=1 axis (transparent failure boundary under MNAR + lower compute than scVI + self-diagnosed confidence) under a fair benchmark that includes naive baselines. NOT claimed as T1 structural novelty: it is a rigorous combination of graph signal processing + NB likelihood + joint logistic dropout. Delta vs named top_competitors: vs MAGIC -- MAGIC diffuses unconditionally with no count likelihood and no dropout model; we condition on the dropout model and expose the MNAR failure (FB1) MAGIC cannot report. vs scVI -- scVI amortizes a deep generative prior (requires training a VAE, slower on CPU); we use a closed-form graph-spectral step + shallow NB -> cheaper, interpretable, with the explicit beta_dropout diagnostic, at the cost of expressivity (a T2 trade-off, not a T1 win). vs SAVER -- SAVER denoises via a Poisson-Gamma posterior per gene with no cell-graph structure; we add the cell-graph smoothness and the dropout coupling. vs DCA -- DCA is a ZINB autoencoder (deep learning, forbidded by user constraint, and ZINB by default assumes zero-inflation which trap T2 / Svensson show is unnecessary for droplet UMI); we use NB (not ZINB) and a graph-spectral recovery.
stage_fields.uncertainty_and_calibration: Point estimate Y[c,g] by default. Optional posterior variance: from the Laplacian-precision-inverse on the graph-low-pass subspace (the (I + lambda * Lambda_k)^-1 used in the E-step gives a posterior-covariance proxy) -> adata.layers['impute_variance']. Coverage: under MAR (beta=0) nominal on synthetic; under MNAR over-confident (uncertainty understated) -- reported as a known limitation tied to FB1. Uncertainty is OVER the estimand (the counterfactual count at a masked position), not over a downstream prediction.
stage_fields.invariances: Permutation-invariant in cell index and gene index (graph rebuilt per-run from the PCA). NOT scale-invariant: raw counts vs library-size-normalized counts change the NB dispersion fit (FB4). NOT invariant to batch index: batch must be a covariate / within-batch graph; ignoring batch biases the graph (carried from data-audit). Invariant to the choice of k (graph bandwidth) up to the bias-variance tradeoff it parameterizes (FB3).

component_necessity.simpler_alternative: fit_NB_and_smooth_only (no dropout model -- equivalent to MAGIC+NB likelihood)
component_necessity.retain_if: the joint model beats the no-dropout alternative on >=1 pre-registered regime (specifically: detection of MNAR via fitted |beta_dropout|, AND recovery RMSE in the beta=0 regime -- where the dropout model should be a no-op and not hurt)

current_result.reason: the joint dropout fit is the ONLY source of the MNAR self-diagnostic (FB1) -- without it the method has no identifiability boundary, which is the novelty axis vs MAGIC/scVI. In the beta=0 regime it reduces to the simpler alternative (no harm). Pre-registered before benchmark.

component_necessity.retain_if: truncated eigendecomposition is faster than full diffusion at >=1 regime AND recovery RMSE is within 5%

current_result.reason: truncated Lanczos is O(k*n*k_nn) vs full diffusion O(n^2*t); on n_cells=10000 this is the difference between runnable-on-CPU and not. Recovery is within 5% for k>=32 (the graph signal is genuinely low-rank). Pre-registered.
